name: Gospel of Thomas
summary:
The Gospel of Thomas is a Coptic-language early Christian non-canonical gospel, part of the Nag Hammadi library, created circa 1000.

    As one of the earliest Christian texts to survive from ancient Egypt, it provides valuable insights into the diversity of early Christian thought and practice. Composed in Greek but preserved in Coptic, this enigmatic text has fascinated scholars for centuries with its unique blend of mysticism, parables, and apocalyptic visions.

    Its significance extends beyond academic circles, as it speaks to fundamental questions about Jesus' teachings, the nature of God, and the relationship between faith and reason. The Gospel of Thomas continues to inspire artists, writers, and thinkers today, offering a window into the spiritual landscape of early Christianity.
